items.t: Cached and Confused: Web Cache Deception in the Wild
items.s: Web cache deception exploits path confusion: a URL such as /account.php/nonexistent.jpg looks static to a caching proxy but resolves to a private page at the origin, so the cache stores it for any attacker to fetch. A measurement of 340 top sites found leaked personal data, session and CSRF tokens, plus five path-confusion variants that widen the attack.

items.t: Cross-Site Leaks
items.s: The browser HTTP cache answers cross-site questions: evict a resource with a POST or an overlong Referer, make the victim load a target page, then re-probe to see whether it got cached. That reveals whether the page requested a given resource, leaking group membership, search hits and other private state; partitioned caches and SameSite cookies mitigate it.

videos.videoTitle: Ben Sadeghipour - Owning The Clout Through Server Side Request Forgery - DEF CON 27 Conference

items.t: Owning The Clout Through Server Side Request Forgery
items.s: Server-side HTML to PDF generators render attacker markup in the server's own context, so an injected iframe or an escape from a style tag turns the export feature into server-side request forgery that reaches cloud metadata. WeasyPrint's attachment link embeds local files into the output PDF, and DNS rebinding defeats same-origin checks under headless Chrome, yielding cloud keys.

items.t: Hacking Jenkins Part 2 - Abusing Meta Programming for Unauthenticated RCE!
items.s: Jenkins validated pipeline scripts by handing them to the Groovy parser, but Groovy compile-time meta-programming executes code while parsing. An unauthenticated attacker uses @GrabResolver and @Grab so Grape fetches a JAR from their own server whose service Runner runs on load, giving remote code execution the script-security sandbox never sees.

items.t: Google Search XSS
items.s: Explains how a Google Search XSS was found: fuzzing pairs of HTML tags through different parsing paths and diffing what a sandboxed iframe, DOMParser and createHTMLDocument produce, which exposes noscript and noembed parsing differently when scripting is disabled. The resulting parser differential mutates sanitized markup into script execution and bypassed two sanitizers.

items.t: All is XSS that comes to the .NET
items.s: ASP.NET still accepts a cookieless session segment such as (A(...)) anywhere in a URL path, and Control.ResolveUrl copies that attacker-controlled segment into every app-root-relative URL it emits. Injecting a quote and an event handler there escapes the src or href attribute for XSS, with ES6 template literals supplying payloads that need no parentheses, plus or slash.

items.t: Exploring Continuous Integration Services as a Bug Bounty Hunter
items.s: Public continuous-integration build logs on Travis CI, Circle CI and GitLab CI expose secrets belonging to bug bounty targets and their organisation members. The authors automated pulling logs through the vendor APIs and grepping them at scale, recovering GitHub access tokens with write access to company repositories and deployment SSH keys.

videos.videoTitle: Orange Tsai - Infiltrating Corporate Intranet Like NSA Preauth RCE - DEF CON 27 Conference
HITCON CMT 2019 - Infiltrating Corporate Intranet Like NSA - Pre-auth RCE on Leading SSL VPNs

items.t: Infiltrating Corporate Intranet Like NSA: Pre-Auth RCE On Leading SSL VPNs
items.s: Pre-auth remote code execution chains against Fortigate and Pulse Secure SSL VPNs: traversal file reads, a heap overflow in the web proxy, an undocumented password-reset key, and command injection through a flaw in Pulse's Perl I/O redirection guard. Stolen session databases defeat two-factor auth, and the logon-script feature turns the VPN into a way to compromise every connected client.

items.t: Microsoft Edge (Chromium) - Elevation of Privilege to Potential RCE
items.s: Chromium Edge's new tab page is a remote MSN page holding privileged chrome APIs, and unsanitised top-site titles gave script execution inside it. Calling the undocumented chrome.qbox.navigate with a null url crashed the browser exploitably, and an XSS on an MSN subdomain set a cookie that poisoned the cached new tab page for persistent takeover.

items.t: Exploiting Null Byte Buffer Overflow for a $40,000 bounty
items.s: A registration form passed a user string and its length to a back-end C routine; null bytes were stripped in transit but the length was not, so the C side read past the shortened string. Repeating a POST full of %00 bytes returned megabytes of adjacent server memory, including RSA private keys, other users' page DOMs, plaintext credentials and internal HTTP requests.

items.note: community favourite - excluded from the top 10

videos.videoTitle: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn
albinowax - HTTP Desync Attacks: Smashing into the Cell Next Door - DEF CON 27 Conference

items.t: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling Reborn
items.s: Revives HTTP request smuggling by making front-end and back-end servers disagree about where a request ends, using conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers hidden by parser quirks. Timing-based detection makes testing safe, and the poisoned socket lets an attacker prepend content to other users' requests, steal credentials, poison caches and reach internal endpoints.

items.t: Facebook Messenger server random memory exposure through corrupted GIF
items.s: A malformed GIF declared a canvas but omitted image data, causing Facebook Messenger’s server-side renderer to fill the output with uninitialized memory. Repeated uploads produced different images containing fragments left by other server activity, demonstrating a remote information leak through image processing.

videos.videoTitle: [CB19] Let's Make Windows Defender Angry: Antivirus can be an oracle! by Ryo Ichikawa

items.t: Let's Make Windows Defender Angry: Antivirus can be an oracle!
items.s: AVOracle turns Windows Defender into a content-dependent side channel by placing attacker-controlled script fragments around a secret and observing whether the resulting file is flagged. It recovers secrets byte by byte and also abuses Defender’s neutralization behavior to erase log regions or corrupt structured files.

items.t: At Home Among Strangers
items.s: Reverse proxies normally append the real client address to X-Forwarded-For, making a spoofed value harmless. A bare carriage return can make some back ends stop parsing before the proxy-appended addresses and trust the attacker’s value, bypassing IP allowlists.

items.t: Exploiting padding oracles with fixed IVs
items.s: A session token is encrypted with AES-CBC but never signed and uses a fixed IV, so a padding oracle can forge chosen plaintext apart from one uncontrollable random block. Reusing the leading blocks of a freely issued anonymous token moves that junk inside a JSON string, and a second user property placed after it wins in JSON.parse, producing an admin token.

items.t: XSS in GMail's AMP4Email via DOM Clobbering
items.s: AMP4Email in Gmail allowed the id attribute, so DOM clobbering was possible. Two anchors sharing an id yield an HTMLCollection whose members can be addressed by name, and an anchor stringifies to its href, letting an attacker clobber the AMP_MODE and testLocation globals and point AMP's script loader at an attacker URL for XSS.

items.t: Abusing HTTP hop-by-hop request headers
items.s: Naming arbitrary headers in the HTTP Connection header marks them hop-by-hop, and proxies that forward that list instead of consuming it let an attacker delete headers a downstream hop added. Removing X-Forwarded-For can make an application treat the request as internal, and the trick also fingerprints caches, bypasses WAF rules that require a header, and can poison caches with error responses.

videos.videoTitle: Mikhail Egorov - What’s Wrong with WebSocket APIs? Unveiling Vulnerabilities in WebSocket APIs.

items.t: Unveiling vulnerabilities in WebSocket APIs
items.s: The slides survey WebSocket API weaknesses, including cross-site hijacking through weak Origin checks and missing authentication or object-level authorization on messages. They also show how incomplete reverse-proxy upgrade validation can turn a WebSocket tunnel into arbitrary HTTP access to internal endpoints.

items.t: CPDoS: Cache Poisoned Denial of Service
items.s: CPDoS poisons a cache with an error page instead of content: a single request carrying an oversized header, a meta character or a method-override header passes the cache but makes the origin fail. The cache stores the error response and serves it to every later visitor, disabling the resource across a CDN region.

items.t: Security analysis of portal element
items.s: Security review of Chrome's new portal element, which embeds a page that behaves like a top-level frame. It accepted file, chrome and javascript URLs for cross-origin script execution, ignored X-Frame-Options, allowed keyboard-driven clickjacking, leaked cross-site state and open ports by counting onload events, received SameSite cookies, and permitted dangling-markup exfiltration.

items.t: Abusing autoresponders and email bounces
items.s: Autoresponders and delivery bounces return the attacker's own message together with internal details. Filling a Google Drive owner's mailbox made the access-request mail, sent from the attacker's address, bounce back with the owner's address and document title, and a strict DMARC policy on an attacker domain forces a forwarder to bounce and expose the hidden downstream address.

items.t: ESI Injection Part 2: Abusing specific implementations
items.s: Three vendor-specific abuses of injected Edge Side Include tags: an inline fragment writes a fetchable poisoned page into the cache, a remote stylesheet on an include reaches a Java XSLT engine and runs commands, and a newline inside a request-header value injects a Host header for limited SSRF against Oracle Web Cache.

items.t: A Tale of Exploitation in Spreadsheet File Conversions
items.s: Server-side document conversion with LibreOffice is fingerprinted through spreadsheet INFO functions and PDF metadata, then abused because LibreOffice picks the format from file contents, not the extension. An ODS or EPS file renamed to .xlsx reaches OLE xlinks, ODF text sections or Ghostscript, giving local file read and SSRF to cloud metadata; unoconv silently updating links is CVE-2019-17400.

items.t: Reusing Cookies
items.s: SaaS vendors that let customers point a subdomain at them by CNAME often share one session cookie across the vendor domain and every customer domain. An attacker signs up for a trial and retargets his own cookie Domain attribute at a customer subdomain, gaining his account there: phishing and fake login pages, open redirect, stored XSS, and other tenants private documents.

items.t: SSRF Protocol Smuggling in Plaintext Credential Handlers : LDAP
items.s: LDAP client libraries pass CRLF through in the username and password of a plaintext simple bind, so an application letting a user set the LDAP server, port and credentials becomes an SSRF that can speak other plaintext TCP protocols. The example smuggles a whole Redis command sequence in the password field to write a PHP web shell into the web root.

items.t: Exploiting prototype pollution - RCE in Kibana
items.s: Turns prototype pollution into remote code execution in Kibana. A Timelion expression that assigns through an object's prototype pollutes Object.prototype, and Kibana's Canvas then spawns a node child process whose environment the attacker now controls, setting NODE_OPTIONS to require /proc/self/environ so another injected variable runs as JavaScript.

items.t: Exploiting SSRF in AWS Elastic Beanstalk
items.s: An SSRF in an app hosted on AWS Elastic Beanstalk reaches the instance metadata service and steals the default aws-elasticbeanstalk-ec2-role credentials. The default policy permits listing and writing any elasticbeanstalk-* bucket, so the attacker takes the source and drops a webshell in the deployment bucket, which executes once CodePipeline redeploys or the environment is rebuilt or cloned.

items.t: Don't open that XML: XXE to RCE in XML plugins for VS Code, Eclipse, Theia, ...
items.s: The LSP4XML language server parses XML as soon as an editor opens or saves it, so a malicious file triggers an external entity fetch with no further user action. Its DTD cache then writes the downloaded file to a path taken from the entity URL without sanitising it, so a traversal drops an executable into an autostart folder and runs it at next login.

items.t: Finding and Exploiting .NET Remoting over HTTP using Deserialisation
items.s: Servers exposing .NET Remoting over HTTP with TypeFilterLevel set to Full deserialise attacker-supplied SOAP bodies, so ysoserial.net gadgets reach code execution once the Body tags are stripped or a dummy method tag is inserted. Adds safe detection by error message, attacks on clients over unencrypted channels, a crash case, and header and encoding tricks that evade WAFs.

items.t: Getting Shell with XAMLX Files
items.s: Uploading a .XAMLX workflow-service file to an IIS application runs code, either through XAML deserialisation gadgets wrapped in an Array element at compile time or through inline C# and expression activities evaluated when the file is requested. A payload can break out of the generated method into the class body, and a web.config can register the handler where it is missing.

items.t: Common Security Issues in Financially-Oriented Web Applications
items.s: An NCC Group guideline cataloguing business-logic flaws specific to e-commerce and financial web applications: TOCTOU and race conditions on balance checks, parameter and currency manipulation, rounding and numeric overflow abuse, voucher, points and refund abuse, hidden backend APIs and test data left in production. The attacker gains money rather than code execution.

items.t: IIS Application vs. Folder Detection During Blackbox Testing
items.s: Requesting a built-in ASP.NET service endpoint such as profile_json_appservice.axd/jsdebug under any path reveals whether that path is an IIS application, which answers with 200 and JavaScript, or merely a folder, which answers 500. Knowing which decides whether an upload can become code execution via web.config and supplies the application path needed to forge ViewState payloads.

items.t: Exploiting Deserialisation in ASP.NET via ViewState
items.s: ASP.NET signs and encrypts the __VIEWSTATE parameter using machineKey values, so when MAC validation is disabled or the validation and decryption keys leak, an attacker forges a ViewState carrying a serialisation gadget and executes code on the server. Covers a ysoserial.net plugin, legacy .NET behaviour, recovering the application path, __EVENTVALIDATION, and WAF evasion.

videos.videoTitle: HITCON CMT 2019 - The cookie monster in your browsers

items.t: The Cookie Monster in Your Browsers
items.s: A subdomain can force duplicate cookies onto its parent, while oversized cookies can make servers reject requests and legacy comma splitting can inject additional cookie values. The slides combine these browser/server discrepancies into CSRF token fixation, HttpOnly bypasses, and theft of OAuth authorization codes from blocked redirects.

items.t: DOMPurify 2.0.0 bypass using mutation XSS
items.s: A Chrome and Safari parsing quirk re-serializes markup so content nested inside an svg element jumps out of it when innerHTML is assigned to itself. Markup that DOMPurify judges harmless on first parse therefore mutates into an img carrying an onerror handler and executes script; math and br variants work the same way.

items.t: XSS-Auditor --- the protector of unprotected and the deceiver of protected
items.s: Chrome's XSS Auditor was reverted from block mode to filter mode, so instead of stopping a page it silently strips the matched script. Reflecting a fake match aimed at a page's own defensive script deletes that script, and a CTF write-up shows this turning an otherwise blocked injection into working XSS.

items.t: Get pwned by scanning QR Code
items.s: Firefox for iOS executed javascript URIs supplied by its built-in QR code scanner, so scanning a crafted code ran script in the context of the page the user was already viewing and could read its contents and cookies. It also worked in reader mode, on local files and internal pages, and ignored the site's content security policy. Opera Mini for iOS was affected too.

items.t: Remote Code Execution via Insecure Deserialization in Telerik UI
items.s: Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX takes the object type from its encrypted rauPostData upload parameter and hands it to JavaScriptSerializer. After breaking the hard-coded upload encryption key and uploading a mixed mode assembly DLL, an attacker names AssemblyInstaller as the type and points its Path at that DLL, so loading it runs native code and returns a reverse shell.

videos.videoTitle: The world of Site Isolation and compromised renderer

items.t: The world of Site Isolation and compromised renderer
items.s: Assuming a compromised Chrome renderer, the slides find browser-process trust gaps in postMessage, protocol handlers, Reader mode, and extension message channels. Chained with permissive extension APIs, these gaps enable cross-site data reads, arbitrary file-URL access, credential theft, CSP bypass, and broader Site Isolation escapes.

videos.videoTitle: G1234! - SSO Wars: The Token Menace - Alvaro Munoz & Oleksandr Mirosh
Alvaro Muñoz - SSO Wars: The Token Menace - DEF CON 27 Conference
SSO Wars: The Token Menace

items.t: SSO Wars: The Token Menace
items.s: Two flaws in .NET single sign-on. An unvalidated algorithm name from a JWT header or an XML SignatureMethod reaches CryptoConfig, letting an attacker instantiate arbitrary types; Dupe Key Confusion adds a second KeyInfo element so signature validation uses the attacker's own key. Lets an attacker forge SAML assertions and log in as any user, plus denial of service and code execution.

videos.videoTitle: HostSplit: Exploitable Antipatterns in Unicode Normalization

items.t: HostSplit: Exploitable Antipatterns in Unicode Normalization
items.s: Some Unicode characters normalise under NFKC to ASCII with URL syntax meaning, so a hostname validated as a subdomain of a trusted site resolves as a different host plus a path, bypassing allow-lists and stealing OAuth tokens. HostBond is the reverse: punycode decoded for display lets an attacker domain render as a trusted host or email sender.

items.t: Backchannel Leaks on Strict Content-Security Policy
items.s: Under a strict default-src 'self' policy the browser still allows outbound requests to unapproved hosts. Chrome does not enforce CSP on link rel=prerender, and Chrome, Firefox and Safari all follow a meta http-equiv=refresh redirect, so either tag gives an out-of-band channel for exfiltration and for triggering blind XSS callbacks without JavaScript.

items.t: Uploading web.config for Fun and Profit 2
items.s: Uploading a web.config file into an IIS application root or a subfolder to reach code execution. Managed handlers run the file itself as an ASPX page, AspNetCoreModule sets a process path, machineKey and JSON_AppService reach .NET deserialisation, and compilerOptions writes a web shell from an SMB share. Handler and mimeMap tricks also give stored XSS.

items.t: Exploiting Spring Boot Actuators
items.s: Spring Boot actuator endpoints left unauthenticated are turned into remote code execution. The jolokia endpoint reloads a Logback config from an attacker URL that performs a JNDI lookup, and the env endpoint rewrites Spring properties so that Eureka returns an XStream gadget chain, the datasource runs arbitrary SQL, or a bootstrap location feeds a SnakeYAML deserialization payload.

items.t: Exploiting JNDI Injections in Java
items.s: Java 8u191 stopped JNDI lookups loading remote classes, but a malicious RMI or LDAP server can still return a reference naming Tomcat's BeanFactory as its object factory. BeanFactory builds any bean and its forceString property redirects a setter to an arbitrary one-String method, so targeting javax.el.ELProcessor.eval evaluates attacker expression language and runs commands.

items.t: Apache Solr Injection Research
items.s: Apache Solr parameter injection: an application that pastes unencoded user input into its Solr query lets an attacker smuggle extra parameters such as shards, qt and stream.body, or Solr local parameters like an xmlparser query, and so reach the update and config endpoints. From there it chains to remote code execution, XXE, arbitrary file read and SSRF.

items.t: PHP-FPM RCE(CVE-2019-11043)
items.s: A newline in the URI makes nginx pass an empty PATH_INFO to PHP-FPM, so a pointer calculation underflows and writes a null byte before the buffer, corrupting the FastCGI environment allocator. A following putenv then overwrites a hash-colliding fake request header with PHP_VALUE, letting an unauthenticated attacker set php.ini directives and run commands.

items.t: Bypassing SOP Using the Browser Cache
items.s: The browser cache is keyed only on the absolute URL, with no record of which origin requested it. A JSONP or CORS response cached after a legitimate same-site request is handed back to any site that requests the same URL, so Referer, Origin, SameSite and custom-header checks never run because the request never reaches the server.

videos.videoTitle: Alexey Tiurin - Reverse proxies & Inconsistency

items.t: Reverse proxies & Inconsistency
items.s: Reverse proxies, caches, and origin servers decode and normalize paths differently, especially around path parameters, encoded dot segments, and duplicate slashes. The slides use these parser differentials to bypass access rules, misroute requests, manipulate security headers, and create web cache deception or poisoning.

items.t: x-up-devcap-post-charset Header in ASP.NET to Bypass WAFs Again
items.s: When the User-Agent starts with UP, ASP.NET takes the request body charset from the non-standard x-up-devcap-post-charset header instead of the Content-Type charset directive. An attacker encodes a POST payload in an exotic codepage such as ibm500, so a WAF that only whitelists Content-Type charsets sees nothing while the application decodes the attack.

items.t: Turbo Intruder: Embracing the billion-request attack
items.s: A Burp extension built on a hand-written HTTP stack that sends requests far faster than normal tooling, reaching about 30,000 requests per second and sustaining multi-day attacks at flat memory. Python-scripted attacks, response filtering and a gate that releases requests simultaneously make large brute force and race-condition hunting practical.

videos.videoTitle: NDSS 2020 Cross-Origin State Inference (COSI) Attacks: Leaking Web Site States through XS-Leaks

items.t: Cross-Origin State Inference (COSI) Attacks: Leaking Web Site States through XS-Leaks
items.s: The paper systematizes Cross-Origin State Inference attacks into 40 XS-Leak classes and introduces a postMessage-based leak. Its Basta-COSI tool combines multiple vectors across browsers to distinguish user states, finding login, ownership, account-type, SSO, or access leaks in all 62 tested applications and sites.

videos.videoTitle: USENIX Security '19 - Iframes/Popups Are Dangerous in Mobile WebView: Studying and

items.t: Iframes/Popups Are Dangerous in Mobile WebView: Studying and Mitigating Differential Context Vulnerabilities
items.s: The paper identifies differential context vulnerabilities created when browser iframe and popup assumptions are carried into Android WebView’s different UI, navigation, and API model. DCV-Hunter finds prevalent origin hiding, message-integrity, popup-order, and navigation flaws that enable bridge abuse or phishing, and the proposed WebView changes mitigate them with about 2 ms overhead.

videos.videoTitle: USENIX Security '19 - Leaky Images: Targeted Privacy Attacks in the Web

items.t: Leaky Images: Targeted Privacy Attacks in the Web
items.s: Leaky images let an attacker privately share an authenticated image with a target, embed it cross-site, and infer whether that exact user visited based on load success. The paper extends the technique to group tracking, cross-service pseudonym linking, and scriptless deanonymization, finding vulnerable sharing flows on at least eight of 30 popular services.

items.t: Bypassing CSP with policy injection
items.s: A URL parameter reflected into a CSP report-uri directive lets an attacker append directives to the policy. On Edge a semicolon and underscore make the syntax invalid so the whole policy is dropped, and on Chrome an appended script-src-elem directive overrides the existing script-src, in both cases restoring script execution and turning a blocked injection into working XSS.

videos.videoTitle: NDSS 2019 JavaScript Template Attacks: Automatically Inferring Host Info for Targeted Exploits

items.t: JavaScript Template Attacks: Automatically Inferring Host Information for Targeted Exploits
items.s: An automated method records every property JavaScript can read in many environments and builds templates from them, so a property stable on one system but different on another leaks the host. Two new side channels also reveal the CPU instruction set and the memory allocator, defeating anti-fingerprinting in Firefox, Chrome, Edge and mobile Tor and guiding targeted exploits.

videos.videoTitle: USENIX Security '19 - What Are You Searching For? A Remote Keylogging Attack

items.t: What Are You Searching For? A Remote Keylogging Attack on Search Engine Autocomplete
items.s: KREEP reconstructs search queries from encrypted autocomplete traffic by combining packet timing, URL-space encoding, and HTTP/2 Huffman-compression size leaks with neural and language models. Across two search engines it identified 15% of queries within 50 hypotheses and recovered up to 60% of query text; randomized padding or merged requests reduced the leakage.

items.t: Cross-Site Challenge-Response Attacks
items.s: Brute-forces password and secret-code challenge-response checks across origins by making visitors' browsers submit guesses and reading success from side channels that survive the same-origin policy. One variant turns any page visitor into a guessing bot, another targets the visitor's own account; a survey finds the weakness in popular sites, CMSs, routers and IoT devices.

videos.videoTitle: PhishFarm: A Scalable Framework for Measuring the Effectivness of Evasion Techniques Against...
videos.channel: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

items.t: PhishFarm: A Scalable Framework for Measuring the Effectiveness of Evasion Techniques against Browser Phishing Blacklists
items.s: PhishFarm deploys 2,380 live PayPal-branded decoy phishing sites on fresh .com domains, each behind one of six request filters taken from real phishing kits, reports them to 10 anti-phishing entities and times browser blacklisting. Cloaking by geolocation, device type or JavaScript cut the chance of blacklisting by over 55 percent, and mobile browsers failed to warn at all.

videos.videoTitle: USENIX Security '19 - All Your Clicks Belong to Me: Investigating Click Interception on the Web

items.t: All Your Clicks Belong to Me: Investigating Click Interception on the Web
items.s: OBSERVER instruments Chromium to detect third-party scripts that rewrite links, attach click handlers, mimic first-party content, or place transparent overlays over it. A crawl of the Alexa top 250,000 found 437 scripts intercepting clicks on 613 sites, often for ad monetization and sometimes redirecting users to scamware or drive-by downloads.

videos.videoTitle: NDSS 2019 Latex Gloves: Protecting Browser Extensions from Probing and Revelation Attacks

items.t: Latex Gloves: Protecting Browser Extensions from Probing and Revelation Attacks
items.s: Browser extensions give themselves away: a page can probe web-accessible resources by URL, and an extension that injects a WAR reference into the page reveals Firefox per-profile random UUID. Combining revelation with probing uniquely identifies about 90 percent of content-injecting extensions and yields a stable per-browser tracking identifier.

videos.videoTitle: USENIX Security '19 - Scalable Scanning and Automatic Classification of TLS Padding Oracle

items.t: Scalable Scanning and Automatic Classification of TLS Padding Oracle Vulnerabilities
items.s: The paper reduces a broad TLS malformed-record probe set to a scalable scan and clusters response fingerprints to group related implementations. Scanning the Alexa Top Million found CBC padding oracles on 1.83% of sites, including nearly 100 variants and exploitable cases distinguishable through TLS alerts or TCP behavior without precise timing.

videos.videoTitle: Postcards from the Post HTTP World: Amplification of HTTPS Vulnerabilities in the Web Ecosystem
videos.channel: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

items.t: Postcards from the Post-HTTP World: Amplification of HTTPS Vulnerabilities in the Web Ecosystem
items.s: A crawl of the Alexa top 10k plus 90,816 dependency and sub-domain hosts maps still-exploitable TLS flaws such as ROBOT, DROWN, POODLE-TLS and Heartbleed onto attack trees, then measures the web-application damage. 898 sites become fully compromisable, 412 can have every session cookie stolen and 543 accept forced cookies, usually via a vulnerable related domain or script host.

videos.videoTitle: USENIX Security '19 - The Betrayal At Cloud City: An Empirical Analysis Of Cloud-Based Mobile

items.t: The Betrayal at Cloud City: An Empirical Analysis of Cloud-Based Mobile Backends
items.s: SkyWalker extracts backend URLs from Android apps, fingerprints operating-system, service, application, and transport layers, assigns ownership, and verifies known and web-application flaws. On the top 5,000 free Google Play apps, it found 983 N-day and 655 zero-day instances and maps them to upgrade, patch, block, report, or migrate actions.

items.t: Provoking browser quirks with behavioural fuzzing
items.s: Behavioural fuzzing drives every Unicode code point into a chosen HTML or JavaScript position and diffs the parse result to expose browser quirks. In Firefox it shows a newline closing an HTML comment after an incomplete terminator, a null byte opening one, and certain code points being ignored by the JavaScript parser, each yielding a new filter-bypass XSS vector.

videos.videoTitle: Measuring and Analyzing Search Engine Poisoning of Linguistic Collisions
videos.channel: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

items.t: Measuring and Analyzing Search Engine Poisoning of Linguistic Collisions
items.s: Misspellings that happen to be real words, often in another language, slip past search engines' auto-correction, so attackers can rank malicious pages against those queries. A crawl of 1.77 million misspelled searches on Google and Baidu, with a neural model to pick candidates, finds about 1.19 percent return malicious first-page results, concentrated in gambling, drugs and adult terms.

items.t: Telerik Revisited
items.s: Re-examines CVE-2017-11317 in Telerik UI for ASP.NET and finds it is more than an arbitrary file upload: the rauPostData blob carries an assembly-qualified type name handed to JavaScriptSerializer, giving arbitrary deserialization. Using AssemblyInstaller to load a mixed-mode DLL runs its DllMain, so unauthenticated code execution needs no write access to the web root.

items.t: Re-Animating ActivitySurrogateSelector
items.s: Microsoft's .NET 4.8 fix for the ActivitySurrogateSelector deserialization gadget is only a type check that a hidden app setting can disable. A still-working gadget, TextFormattingRunProperties driving XamlReader and ObjectDataProvider, sets that flag or writes the internal boolean by reflection, re-enabling arbitrary assembly loading and code execution from a deserialization sink.

items.t: Practical Decryption exFiltration: Breaking PDF Encryption
items.s: Modified encrypted PDFs exfiltrate plaintext when their recipients decrypt them. Partial encryption permits attacker-controlled forms, links or scripts to reference encrypted objects; unauthenticated CBC and known permission bytes also enable encrypted gadgets. Tests on 27 viewers distinguish interaction requirements and full, partial or single-word leakage.

items.t: The inception bar: a new phishing method
items.s: Demonstrates a fake address bar after mobile Chrome hides its toolbar during scrolling. A nested scrolling region and top-boundary reset keep the real toolbar hidden as the user scrolls upward. The technique needs an initial user scroll and matching browser behavior; it does not change the actual origin or require fullscreen permission.

items.t: Bypassing GitHub's OAuth flow
items.s: The article explains an OAuth authorization bypass caused by Rails routing HEAD requests like GET while GitHub’s controller treated every non-GET request as an authorization POST. Because HEAD was exempt from CSRF validation, an attacker could issue a cross-site authenticated request that silently granted an OAuth application access to a victim’s GitHub account.

items.t: Detecting incognito mode in Chrome 76 with a timing attack
items.s: The article detects Chrome 76 Incognito mode by repeatedly timing FileSystem API writes, exploiting the speed and variance difference between its memory-backed Incognito storage and disk-backed normal storage. Measurements showed markedly faster, less noisy writes in Incognito, though the technique is slow and sensitive to hardware and background activity.

items.t: Adblock Plus filter lists may execute arbitrary code in web pages
items.s: The article shows how Adblock Plus’s `$rewrite` option let filter-list maintainers redirect Fetch or XHR code loads through same-origin open redirects, enabling arbitrary JavaScript execution in affected pages. It documents the affected extensions, Google-service examples, and mitigations including CSP and removal of the feature.

items.t: Subverting Electron Apps via Insecure Preload
items.s: The article categorizes four ways Electron preload scripts can undermine renderer isolation, including leaked Node globals, dangerous exported functions, sandbox bypasses, and prototype tampering without context isolation. Wire and Discord case studies turn renderer code execution into arbitrary file writes or privileged IPC leading to native command execution.

items.t: Remote Code Execution on most Dell computers
items.s: The article chains Dell SupportAssist’s privileged localhost web API, reusable command signatures, weak Dell-origin checks, DNS interception, and a URL-normalization bypass into remote code execution. A malicious page can make the agent download an attacker-substituted executable from an allowlisted HTTP hostname and run it as Administrator.

items.t: Zoom Zero Day: 4 Million Webcams & maybe an RCE? Just get them to visit your website!
items.s: The report finds that Zoom’s persistent macOS localhost server let any visited website force the client into a meeting, optionally activating the webcam, and repeatedly launch calls for denial of service. It also shows the service could silently reinstall Zoom and evaluates how weak signatures, same-NAT conditions, and trusted download domains left drive-by attack paths.

items.t: Abusing PHP query string parser to bypass IDS, IPS, and WAF
items.s: The article maps PHP’s normalization of query-string parameter names, including whitespace, brackets, null bytes, and encoded underscores, into application-visible keys. That parser differential lets crafted requests evade IDS, IPS, and WAF rules while reaching the intended PHP parameter, demonstrated by bypassing Suricata rules around Drupalgeddon2.

items.t: DataSpii: The catastrophic data leak via browser extensions
items.s: DataSpii investigates eight Chrome and Firefox extensions that collected browsing URLs, titles, referrers, tokens, and LAN metadata and fed near-real-time analytics sold to subscribers. Controlled extension analysis, decoded traffic, corporate disclosures, and honeypot URLs showed delayed collection, exposure of private and shared-link data, and repeat third-party visits.

items.t: Universal RCE with Ruby YAML.load
items.s: The article adapts a universal Ruby 2.x Marshal deserialization gadget chain to unsafe YAML.load without Rails dependencies. A hand-built YAML object graph drives RubyGems classes through sorting and StubSpecification loading until a pipe-prefixed loaded_from value executes a command.

items.t: Using WebRTC ICE Servers for Port Scanning in Chrome
items.s: The article turns Chrome’s WebRTC ICE server handling into a browser-based LAN scanner. Crafted TURN URLs force TCP probes to arbitrary ports, including normally blocked ones, and icecandidateerror details distinguish reachable hosts and open ports, while mDNS fallback logic helps locate private ranges.

items.t: Why npm lockfiles can be a security blindspot for injecting malicious modules
items.s: The article shows how a malicious pull request can hide a dependency source replacement inside a large yarn.lock or package-lock.json diff, causing installs to fetch and run an attacker-controlled module. It recommends automated lockfile policies, trusted HTTPS registries, tighter review ownership, and avoiding lockfiles for published libraries.

items.t: Jackson gadgets - Anatomy of a vulnerability
items.s: The article develops a Jackson polymorphic-deserialization gadget using Logback’s JDBC connection source, first yielding SSRF through attacker-controlled JDBC URLs. When H2 is present, its remote initialization script and Java alias features extend the chain to code execution; the authors also describe an iterative static taint-analysis tool for gadget discovery.

items.t: GraphQL Batching Attacks
items.s: The article shows how GraphQL batching can pack thousands of operations into one HTTP request, undermining request-based rate limits and monitoring. Examples use batched login and OTP mutations to amplify brute force and bypass authentication controls, with mitigations focused on per-operation limits and business-logic checks.

items.t: Handlebars template injection and RCE in a Shopify app
items.s: Researchers turn server-side Handlebars template injection into RCE by abusing JavaScript constructors, helpers, bind, and prototype mutation to build and invoke a Function body. They demonstrate the chain against Shopify’s Return Magic app and note the Handlebars fix blocking constructor access.

items.t: Automating local DTD discovery for XXE exploitation
items.s: The article automates discovery of reusable local DTD files for XXE exploitation when outbound retrieval of an attacker-hosted DTD is unavailable. DTD Finder inventories packaged DTDs, enumerates overridable entities, tests five injection patterns, and emits working error-based file-read payloads.

items.t: Signature validation bypass in SimpleSAMLphp and XMLSecLibs
items.s: The advisory traces a SimpleSAMLphp/XMLSecLibs signature-validation bypass to an XPath query that accepts Reference elements from multiple SignedInfo nodes while verifying only the first signature. An authenticated identity-provider user can add an unsigned reference to a forged assertion, impersonate any identity, and have it accepted as signed.

items.t: WordPress 5.0.0 Remote Code Execution
items.s: The research chains WordPress post-meta overwrite, image-editor path traversal, and theme template inclusion into authenticated RCE. An author can redirect image processing into the active theme and plant PHP in a crafted image; the article covers Imagick metadata and GD pixel techniques, affected versions, and patch interactions.

items.t: Requests-Racer
items.s: Requests-Racer is a Python transport adapter for synchronizing the completion of multiple HTTP requests, even across destinations and payload sizes, to test web application race conditions. Its documentation covers Requests session integration, timing controls, caveats, and compatibility constraints.

items.t: Hijacking browser TLS traffic through Client Domain Hooking
items.s: The article introduces Client Domain Hooking, a MITM technique that uses one intercepted clear-text request to keep a browser communicating through an attacker-controlled domain and reverse proxy while preserving trusted TLS. It also announces a study finding that 80% of the reviewed browser-based applications lacked HSTS.

items.t: Permanent URL Hijack Through 301 HTTP Redirect Cache Poisoning
items.s: The article shows how a network attacker can answer one clear-text HTTP request with a cacheable 301 redirect, persistently steering later browser visits to an attacker-controlled HTTPS reverse proxy. It explores cross-origin cache behavior, redirect-chain automation, and limits imposed by HSTS preload, HTTPS-first navigation, and existing cached entries.

items.t: Switcheroo: Windows SSDP Blind SSRF
items.s: Switcheroo shows how a LAN attacker can answer Windows SSDP discovery, then use an HTTP 301 redirect to make the target issue a blind GET to an arbitrary host, including localhost. The write-up demonstrates the blind SSRF primitive on several Windows versions and discusses its use against local REST APIs.

items.t: Using HTTP Pipelining to hide requests
items.s: The article uses HTTP/1.1 pipelining to send a benign and a second, different-host request over one TLS connection, concealing the latter’s hostname from observers who cannot decrypt traffic. Testing found the technique worked across AWS CloudFront, while Cloudflare rejected the mismatched Host because it bound requests to the connection’s SNI.

items.t: NGINX error_page request smuggling
items.s: The whitepaper demonstrates that an NGINX `error_page` configuration which redirects to an absolute URL can reinterpret a GET body as a pipelined request. The smuggled request can cross virtual-host boundaries or desynchronize an upstream load balancer; using a named error location is presented as a workaround.

items.t: Fun with URI Handlers
items.s: The article shows how a custom Origin URI passes attacker-controlled text into a Windows command line, permitting argument injection despite quoting. Injected Qt plugin-path arguments load a DLL from a remote share for code execution, while crafted .url shortcuts bypass modern browser encoding and can also suppress updates or spawn extra Origin instances.
